package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of Apache Struts contain a vulnerability (CVE-2023-50164) in the file upload mechanism that allows attackers to manipulate file upload parameters, perform path traversal, and overwrite arbitrary files on the server. This can lead to remote code execution, unauthorized data access, and full system compromise.

execution_context.file_location: MultiPartRequestWrapper component (Java class handling file uploads)
required_permissions: potentially network if code execution is achieved

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Processes user-supplied file upload parameters without proper sanitization, allowing path traversal (e.g., '../../webapps/ROOT/shell.jsp') and arbitrary file overwrite.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code trusts user-supplied file names and paths, allowing attackers to specify file paths outside the intended upload directory. This enables overwriting critical files or placing web shells.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal file upload handlers should sanitize and restrict file paths to prevent traversal and ensure files are only written to safe, intended directories. This code fails to do so.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate file upload code would use strict validation and canonicalization of file paths, rejecting any input with traversal sequences.
key_indicators: Direct use of user-supplied file names/paths
Lack of path sanitization or canonicalization
Ability to write files outside the intended upload directory

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a file upload request with a malicious file name containing path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../webapps/ROOT/shell.jsp').
attack_chain.leads_to: The server processes the upload and writes the file to an attacker-controlled location.

attack_chain.action: Malicious file (e.g., a web shell or script) is placed in a web-accessible directory or overwrites a critical configuration file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can now execute arbitrary code or commands on the server by accessing the uploaded file.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote code execution, leading to data exfiltration, privilege escalation, or full system compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: complete control over the affected system.

behavioral_signatures: File uploads resulting in files being written outside the intended upload directory
Unexpected file types (e.g., .jsp, .php, .sh) appearing in web-accessible directories
Unusual file write operations during file upload requests
file_indicators: Presence of web shells (e.g., shell.jsp, cmd.jsp) in web root or application directories
Files with names containing traversal sequences (e.g., '../../') in server logs
Unexpected overwrites of configuration or executable files
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to file upload endpoints with suspicious file names or paths
Subsequent HTTP GET/POST requests to newly uploaded files (e.g., web shells)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor file upload endpoints for file names containing path traversal patterns (../ or ..\). Audit file system changes for files written outside expected upload directories, especially in web root or configuration locations. Alert on uploads of executable file types (e.g., .jsp, .php) and on access to such files immediately after upload. Review server logs for anomalous file write operations and unexpected file access patterns.
